scenes.title: A city falling asleep
scenes.purpose: Hook: date, place and scale; plant at the edge of a sleeping city.
scenes.visual: Charcoal blueprint of the plant draws on bone paper with a faint grid; a wisp of ochre ink rises from the vent and the page tilts down into a skyline of lit windows that begin to dim into sleep.

transition_out.continuity: plant outline in the foreground becomes the tank cutaway's frame

scenes.narration: The second of December, nineteen eighty-four. In Bo-pahl, central India, almost nine hundred thousand people were falling asleep. At the edge of the city stood a pesticide factory.

layout.portrait: Plant schematic top 55%, skyline low third, date and ledger line in the safe copy block.

beats.action: grid and plant outline begin to draw
camera drops to skyline; 'about 894,000 people' ledger line
windows dim one by one; plant stays lit at the edge
ochre wisp curls from the vent

scenes.title: The tank and the failing safeguards
scenes.purpose: Show what was in the tank and that pressure began to climb. Then: Water ingress is disputed; the safeguards were not working.
scenes.visual: Tank E610 cutaway in fine line; liquid level fills in slate wash; a hand-drawn pressure dial needle creeps from green zone toward brick red; a label stamps '42 tons'. Then: Three small safeguard drawings (cooling coil, scrubber, flare tower) each get a slow pen strike-through; a pipe with a drawn question mark hangs over the tank with the words 'accident? sabotage?' disputed.

transition_out.continuity: the dial needle rises into the top of the next frame as the ink wisp

scenes.narration: Inside, an underground tank held forty-two tons of METH-il eye-so-SIGH-uh-nate, a chemical used to make a pesticide called SEV-in. That night, the pressure in the tank began to climb. How water reached the tank is still disputed. What is not disputed is that the safeguards were failing. The cooling had been off since nineteen eighty-two. The scrubber was on standby. The flare tower was too small.

layout.portrait: Tank centred upper 60%, dial lower-left overlapping, label stack right. Then: Tank top; three safeguard cards stack down the middle; copy lines align left.

beats.action: 'SEVIN pesticide' tag draws on a side arrow
needle starts creeping; dial shakes slightly
pipe and question mark draw over tank

scenes.title: The cloud and the waking
scenes.purpose: The emotional peak: the gas escapes over sleeping streets and the siren is cut. Then: Human scale: people wake and run; thousands dead within days.
scenes.visual: Ochre ink blooms from the vent through a displaced mask, drifts down and soaks across the skyline; windows go out wave by wave; a siren icon pulses once and is crossed out; '~30 tonnes' ledger entry. Then: Small ink figures (silhouette strokes, no faces) run across the stained streets; a few windows re-light then are overtaken; ledger line 'Within days: thousands'.

transition_out.continuity: the figures dissolve into the dots of the next scene

scenes.narration: Near one in the morning, the gas escaped. About thirty tonnes drifted over sleeping streets in under an hour. A siren sounded briefly, and was switched off. People woke choking, their eyes burning. Hundreds of thousands ran into the dark. Within days, thousands were dead.

layout.portrait: Cloud descends from top; skyline low; ledger entries in bottom copy block. Then: Street band mid-frame, figures flowing across; ledger text above.

beats.action: ink bloom begins at the vent
cloud reaches rooftops; windows extinguish in waves
siren icon pulses, then strikes out
'~30 tonnes, under an hour' ledger entry
a window lights; a figure leans out
streams of small figures run left to right

scenes.title: Nobody agrees
scenes.purpose: The count is disputed: government vs survivor groups.
scenes.visual: On the stained page a ledger writes 3,787 (GOVERNMENT) and a dot field fills with ink dots flowing past it toward ~23,000 (SURVIVOR GROUPS); a bracket labelled 'exposed: 500,000+' draws around the page.

transition_out.continuity: the page stays; the ledger turns over to a new line

scenes.narration: Nobody agrees on how many. The government confirms three thousand, seven hundred and eighty-seven. Survivor groups count nearly twenty-three thousand.

layout.portrait: Two big numbers stacked, dots filling between; source tags under each number.

beats.action: dot field floods past the number

scenes.title: Partial justice
scenes.purpose: 1989 settlement, 2010 convictions, Anderson never faced an Indian court.
scenes.visual: Three ledger stamps in sequence: 1989 US$470 MILLION; 2010 seven figures, '2 YEARS'; an empty chair outline with 'WARREN ANDERSON' and a dashed line that ends before it reaches a courtroom door.

transition_out.continuity: the chair outline dissolves into the plant outline of the last scene

scenes.narration: In nineteen eighty-nine, Union Carbide paid four hundred and seventy million dollars to settle. In twenty ten, seven former employees were convicted of negligence. The company's chief, Warren Anderson, never faced an Indian court.
on_screen_text: Warren Anderson: never faced an Indian court

layout.portrait: Three stacked ledger bands; chair outline in the last band.

beats.action: empty chair outline draws; dashed line approaches and stops

scenes.title: Still here
scenes.purpose: Today: waste removed in Jan 2025; over 100,000 survivors still ill; the stain remains. Ends quieter.
scenes.visual: Trucks leave the plant outline in a slow dotted line off the page; dawn skyline wash in pale slate with a few windows lit; the ochre stain stays on the paper; final hold with the title.
scenes.narration: In January twenty twenty-five, hundreds of tonnes of waste were finally trucked out of the factory. More than a hundred thousand survivors still live with chronic illness. For them, that night has not ended.
on_screen_text: The Night Bhopal Didn't Wake Up

layout.portrait: Dawn skyline bottom; trucks line top; end card centred in safe area with 3 s hold.

beats.action: 'JANUARY 2025' types in; trucks dotted line leaves the plant
dawn wash rises; a few windows lit
title end card; hold to end
